Global Well-Posedness and Global Attractor for Two-dimensional Zakharov-Kuznetsov Equation

Minjie Shan Note: Corresponding author. The author was supported by CSC, grant 201606010025 Affiliation: School of Mathematical Sciences, Peking University, Beijing 100871, P.R. China Affiliation:  Emails: smj@pku.edu.cn
Abstract

The initial value problem for two-dimensional Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation is shown to be globally well-posed in Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({{\mathbb{R}}^{2}}) for all 57<s<1\frac{5}{7}<s<1 via using II-method in the context of atomic spaces. By means of the increment of modified energy, the exsitence of global attractor for weakly damped, forced Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation is also established in Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({{\mathbb{R}}^{2}}) for 1011<s<1\frac{10}{11}<s<1.

Keywords: Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation, Global well-posedness, Global attractor, II-method, Atomic spaces.

1 Introduction and Main Results

We consider the Cauchy problem for the symmetrized two-dimensional Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equation

{ut+(∂3x+∂3y)u+(∂x+∂y)u2=0,(x,y)∈ℝ2,t⩾0u⁡(x,y,0)=u0​(x,y)∈Hs​(ℝ2),\left\{\begin{aligned} &u_{t}+(\partial^{3}_{x}+\partial^{3}_{y})u+(\partial_{x}+\partial_{y})u^{2}=0,\ \ \ (x,y)\in{\mathbb{R}}^{2},\ t\geqslant 0\quad\\ &u(x,y,0)=u_{0}(x,y)\in H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}),\\ \end{aligned}\right. (1.1)

where u=u⁡(x,y,t)u=u(x,y,t) is a real-valued function.

The ZK equation was initially decuded as a model of nonlinear unidirectional ion-acoustic wave propagation in a magnetized plasma by Zakharov and Kuznetsov [16]. It may be treated as a higher dimensional generalization of the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. For more details we refer to the papers [17, 18] about the two-dimensional ZK equation appearing here in physical circumstances.

Eventhough the ZK equation is not completely integrable, there still exists two conserved quantities for the flow of ZK,

M⁡(u)​(t)=∫ℝ2u2​(x,y,t)​𝑑x​𝑑y=∫ℝ2u02​(x,y)​𝑑x​𝑑y=M⁡(u0)\displaystyle M(u)(t)=\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{2}}u^{2}(x,y,t)dxdy=\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{2}}u^{2}_{0}(x,y)dxdy=M(u_{0}) (1.2)

and

E⁡(u)​(t)=∫ℝ212​|∇u|2−12​∂xu​∂yu−13​u3​𝑑x​𝑑y=E⁡(u0).\displaystyle E(u)(t)=\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{2}}\frac{1}{2}|\nabla u|^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\partial_{x}u\partial_{y}u-\frac{1}{3}u^{3}dxdy=E(u_{0}). (1.3)

Faminskii [6] firstly obtained the local well-posedness for the two-dimensional ZK equation in the energy space H1​(ℝ2)H^{1}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) by making use of local smoothing effects together with a maximal function estimate for the linearized equation. This method was inspired by the one given by Kenig, Ponce and Vega [12] when dealing with the local well-posedness for KdV equation. With the help of the L2L^{2} and H1H^{1} conservation laws, he proved the global well-posedness for ZK equation additionally. Following this idea, Linares and Pastor [19] optimized the proof of Faminskii to show local well-posedness in Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) for s>34s>\frac{3}{4}. Grünrock and Herr [9] along with Molinet and Pilod [21] proved the local well-posedness in a larger data spaces Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) for s>12s>\frac{1}{2} by taking advantage of the Fourier restriction norm method and one kind of sharp Strichartz estimates. On the basis of the method of Grünrock and Herr, in [25] we recently improved the local well-posedness result to B2,112​(ℝ2)B^{\frac{1}{2}}_{2,1}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) via applying frequency decomposion as well as atomic spaces introduced by Koch and Tataru. Actually, it is L. Molinet and D. Pilod who originality applied this crucial tool of atomic spaces to ZK equation. They obtained the global well-posedness for ZK equation in Hs​(ℝ3)H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{3}) for s>1s>1 by using the conservation laws, doubling time, the argument of Bourgain (see [2]) and atomic spaces. What’s more, as the other part of the same paper [25] we utilized II-method to prove global well-posedness in Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) for 1113<s<1\frac{11}{13}<s<1.

As mentioned above, ZK equation is an asymptotic description of the propagation of nonlinear ion-acoustic wave in a magnetized plasma. However, one cannot totally neglect external excitation and energy dissipation mechanism in reality (see [1], [23] and [29]). Therefore, we would like to consider the following Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation with weak dissipation and forcing terms

{ut+(∂3x+∂3y)u+(∂x+∂y)u2+γu=f,(x,y)∈ℝ2,t⩾0u⁡(x,y,0)=u0​(x,y)∈Hs​(ℝ2),\left\{\begin{aligned} &u_{t}+(\partial^{3}_{x}+\partial^{3}_{y})u+(\partial_{x}+\partial_{y})u^{2}+\gamma u=f,\ \ \ (x,y)\in{\mathbb{R}}^{2},\ t\geqslant 0\quad\\ &u(x,y,0)=u_{0}(x,y)\in H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}),\\ \end{aligned}\right. (1.4)

where the damping parameter γ\gamma is a positive constant and the external forcing term f∈H1​(ℝ2)f\in H^{1}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) is independent of tt.

Global attractor is a bounded subset which is invariant by the flow and attracts all trajectories when tt approaches to +∞+\infty under the corresponding topology. Moise and Rosa studied the regularity of the global attractor of a weakly damped, forced KdV equation in [20]. While Haraux [11] and Goubet [8] proved the asymptotic smoothing effect for dissipative wave equation and nonlinear Schrödinger eqution respectively. As we know that the conservation laws will become invalid in low regularity situation, Colliander, Keel, Staffilani, Takaoka and Tao [3, 4] developed a theory of almost conserved quantities starting with energy in order to extend the local solutions globally in time for dispersive equations. Applying II-method to weakly damped, forced KdV equation, Tsugawa [27] proved the existence of global attractor on Sobolev spaces of negative index. Prashant [24] lately showed an analogue below energy spaces for mKdV equation.

In this article, we refine the global well-posedness for ZK equation through pushing our previous result to 57<s\frac{5}{7}<s. The new ingredient here is a closer investigation into how to use the symmetrization and atomic space to acquire a better control of the modified energy. Whereafter the increment of the modified energy helps us gain the existence of global weak attractor below H1H^{1} for weakly damped, forced ZK equation. The advantage of U2U^{2}, V2V^{2} spaces is to obtain sharp estimates in the time variable, which makes the proof simpler than when we use Xs,1/2+X^{s,1/2+}. For instance, as regards local well-posedness for ZK equation in H12​(ℝ2)H^{\frac{1}{2}}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}), to some extent it corresponds to the non-admissible endpoint Strichartz estimates. However this can be compensated partly by the decay brought from utilizing atomic space. Especially, the use of U2U^{2}, V2V^{2} spaces will assist us to study the problem on the 2D torus or the ℝ×𝕋\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}, which may be nice as a future problem (see also [21] for ZK equation on ℝ×𝕋\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}).

We now state the main results of this paper.

Theorem 1.1.

The initial value problem (1.1) is globally well-posed in Hs​(ℝ2)H^{s}({\mathbb{R}}^{2}) for 57<s<1\frac{5}{7}<s<1.

Remark 1.1. The increment in E⁡(IN​u)E(I_{N}u) on the right hand of (3.16) is N−12N^{-\frac{1}{2}}. One could repeat the almost conservation law argument to prove global well-posedness of (1.1) for all 12<s<1\frac{1}{2}<s<1 upon gaining N−1N^{-1}.

Theorem 1.2.

Let 1011<s<1\frac{10}{11}<s<1. Then, there exists a semigroup A⁡(t)A(t) and maps M1M_{1} and M2M_{2} such that A⁡(t)​u0A(t)u_{0} is the unique solution of (1.4) satisfying

A⁡(t)​u0=M1​(t)​u0+M2​(t)​u0\displaystyle A(t)u_{0}=M_{1}(t)u_{0}+M_{2}(t)u_{0} (1.5)
supt>T1‖M1​(t)​u0‖H1<K\displaystyle\sup\limits_{t>T_{1}}\|M_{1}(t)u_{0}\|_{H^{1}}<K (1.6)

and for t>T1t>T_{1}

‖M2​(t)​u0‖Hs<K​e−γ⁡(t−T1)\displaystyle\|M_{2}(t)u_{0}\|_{H^{s}}<Ke^{-\gamma(t-T_{1})} (1.7)

where T1T_{1} depends on ‖u0‖Hs\|u_{0}\|_{H^{s}}, ‖f‖H1\|f\|_{H^{1}} and γ\gamma, the constant KK depends only on ‖f‖H1\|f\|_{H^{1}} and γ\gamma.

From this theorem, we know that M1​(t)M_{1}(t) is a bounded mapping and M2​(t)M_{2}(t) converges uniformly to 0 in HsH^{s}. It means that the semigroup A⁡(t)A(t) is asymptotically compact in the sense of weak topology. Therefore we gain the existence of the global attractor in HsH^{s} from Theorem 1.1.1 in [26].

Corollary 1.3.

The global weak attractor for (1.4) exisits in HsH^{s} for 1011<s<1\frac{10}{11}<s<1.

Note that

∂t∫u2\displaystyle\partial_{t}\int u^{2} =−2∫u(∂x3+∂y3)u−2∫u(∂x+∂y)u2−2γ∫u2+2∫fu\displaystyle=-2\int u(\partial^{3}_{x}+\partial^{3}_{y})u-2\int u(\partial_{x}+\partial_{y})u^{2}-2\gamma\int u^{2}+2\int fu
=−2γ∫u2+2∫fu\displaystyle=-2\gamma\int u^{2}+2\int fu

Setting h⁡(t)=e2​γ​t​‖u‖L22h(t)=e^{2\gamma t}\|u\|^{2}_{L^{2}} and using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the last term, one can obtain

h′​(t)⩽2​eγ​t​‖f‖L2​h⁡(t).h^{\prime}(t)\leqslant 2e^{\gamma t}\|f\|_{L^{2}}\sqrt{h(t)}.

This implies that

∂th⁡(t)⩽eγ​t​‖f‖L2.\partial_{t}\sqrt{h(t)}\leqslant e^{\gamma t}\|f\|_{L^{2}}.

Hence, we have

‖u‖L2⩽e−γ​t​‖u0‖L2+γ−1​‖f‖L2.\displaystyle\|u\|_{L^{2}}\leqslant e^{-\gamma t}\|u_{0}\|_{L^{2}}+\gamma^{-1}\|f\|_{L^{2}}. (1.8)

Remark 2.2. For the modified energy, we expect a similar exponential decay as (1.8) (see Proposition 4.4).

Remark 3.3. Yang [30] upgrated Tsugawa’s result through lowering −38-\frac{3}{8} to −12-\frac{1}{2} which can be seen as the critical Sobolev index for KdV. However, for ZK equation and mKdV equation it is not easy to find good cancellation of resonant parts as Schrödinger equation (see [5]). Concerning the existence of global attrator, there still are much work to do for these two kinds of equations.

Organization of the paper. In Section 2, we recall some useful propositions and estimates about UpU^{p} and VpV^{p}. Then we prove global well-posedness by using II-method in atomic space in Section 3. Finally, Section 4 is devoted to a prior estimate and the proof of Theorem 1.2.
